Subject: Still tracking Acme HVAC's operations in spreadsheets?

Hi Sarah,

I've been talking to Texas field service companies lately, and I keep hearing the same pattern:

"We track jobs in one system, invoices in another, and pull everything into Excel at the end of the week to see how we're really doing."

Sound familiar?

Here's what I'm seeing: Companies like Acme HVAC aren't missing scheduling software. You're missing **real-time operational visibility**.

What if you could see — right now — which techs are profitable, which jobs are stalled, and whether you're on track for this month's revenue?

No enterprise platform. No 6-month implementation. Just the dashboard you've been building in Excel, but live.

Worth 15 minutes to see how this works?

Cody

P.S. — One of my clients (similar size to Acme HVAC) went from weekly Excel reconciliation to real-time ops dashboards in 60 days. Happy to share the approach.

Campaign Insights

✅ Best Practices

  • •Keep emails under 120 words
  • •Single clear CTA per email
  • •Reference specific pain points
  • •Show credibility briefly

❌ Avoid

  • •“Hope this email finds you well”
  • •Wall of text paragraphs
  • •Multiple competing CTAs
  • •Generic “one-size-fits-all” pitch

💡 Personalization

  • •Research LinkedIn before sending
  • •Reference company growth or news
  • •Adjust pain points to industry
  • •Match tone to recipient seniority
